U0200.d: U0200 means door control module B has dropped off the bus; most makers use B for the front passenger door. For the 2005–2010 Chrysler 300 and Charger, bulletin 08-061-12 names it the passenger door module and replaces it when locks and windows stay dead.
s: Passenger window or lock switch inoperative
Door does not lock or unlock centrally, sometimes intermittent
Child lock or door warning message in the cluster
c: Passenger door module software (Audi Q5 J387 update)
Loose, bent or corroded pins in the door or A-pillar connector
Broken wires in the door hinge harness

U0201.d: U0201 stands for door control module C, in the generic list the next door unit after driver (A) and front passenger (B), so on four-door cars usually a rear door. Audi, for example, gives each rear door its own controller (J388, J389, diagnostic addresses 00BB and 00BC), and its Q3 bulletin 2063376 deals with their child lock motors, but no Audi document names U0201.
s: Rear window, lock or child lock inoperative
Door or child lock warning in the cluster
c: Chafed or broken wires in the rear door hinge harness
Loose or corroded pins in the door connector

U0202.d: U0202 means the body network no longer hears from door control module D, which most four-door layouts give to the right rear door. FCA STAR case S1908000143 (Rev.
s: Right rear window or lock inoperative
Several warning lamps and further U-codes at the same time
Possible no-start or unrequested wiper stroke when the bus wiring is damaged
c: Body harness chafed at the B-pillar or under the seats (FCA minivan)
Broken wires in the rear door hinge harness

U0203.d: U0203 reports a missing door control module E. For the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM fills this slot with the left rear door switch panel, so on these GM platforms E is the electronics behind the rear left window and lock switches rather than a fifth door.
s: Left rear window or lock switches without function
Door locks cycle on their own while driving
Many other lost-communication codes stored at once
c: Instrument panel harness chafed at the steering column (GM Acadia/XT5)
Water at the body control module or in body connectors
Broken wires between rear door and body
Rear door switch panel module faulty

U0204.d: U0204 is set when door control module F stops answering. On the 2011 Saab 9-4x, whose U-code list comes from GM, the letter F belongs to the right rear door switch panel, the mirror-image partner of U0203 on the left.
s: Right rear window or lock switches inoperative
Codes appear together with an instrument self-test when the scan tool is plugged in
c: Spread terminals in the diagnostic connector, false entries while testing (GM)
Broken wires in the right rear door hinge harness
Loose or corroded door connector pins
Rear door switch panel module faulty

U0205.d: U0205 covers door control module G. The generic list reserves eight door module slots, A to H, so G only comes into play on vehicles carrying more door electronics than four side doors; which unit gets the letter is the maker's choice.
s: Window, lock or mirror on the affected door inoperative
Door switch lighting dark
c: Broken or chafed wires at the door transition
Missing fuse, power or ground feed of the door module
Door module faulty or hung after a voltage drop

U0206.d: U0206 indicates that the folding top control module, which drives the hydraulic or electric mechanism of a convertible roof and watches its end positions, has fallen silent on the bus. Lamborghini names U020600, stored in control unit 00C5, in its Revuelto baseline update bulletins L74X-A.11.25 (model year 2024) and L74X-A.05.25 (2025): if the entry shows up during the SVM code step, the technician adds it to the tes
s: Convertible top neither opens nor closes
Roof or top warning in the instrument cluster
c: Module software needs an update after programming (Lamborghini Revuelto)
Fuse, power or ground of the top module missing
Harness or connector in the top compartment damaged or wet

U0207.d: U0207 concerns moveable roof control module A, the electronics of a power sunroof or glass roof. GM uses it: the 2011 Saab 9-5 list names the moveable roof control module, and GM preliminary information PIT5606J (GMC Acadia, Cadillac XT5 2017–2021) counts U0207 among the codes that appear after water gets in – mostly at the upper windshield corners hidden under the glass, rarely past the outer sunroof seal or a drain
s: Sunroof does not respond to the switch
Damp headliner or water marks near the A-pillar
Further U-codes in several modules
c: Water leak at windshield corners, sunroof seal or blocked drain hose
Dash harness chafed at the steering column (GM Acadia/XT5)
Corroded connector at the roof module

U0208.d: U0208 says seat control module A has dropped out, mostly a driver's seat unit. The letter is used differently: FCA radio bulletin 08-108-14 (2015 Cherokee, Grand Cherokee, Ram) calls it the heated seat control module and removes a false U0208-00 on the Cherokee with new Uconnect radio software; Audi bulletin 2067722 (Q7 2017–2024, SQ7) finds U020800 with a dead driver seat when road salt under the driver-side sill ca
s: Power or memory seat does not move
Seat heating or ventilation cannot be switched
Power running boards fail (Ford Expedition/Navigator)
c: Splice under the driver-side carpet corroded by salt water (Audi Q7/Q8)
Seat module or radio software (Ford SSM 55168, FCA 08-108-14)
Seat harness pinched or unplugged under the seat

U0209.d: U0209 means seat control module B is no longer heard. On GM cars of 2010–2015 with heated front seats (LaCrosse, Regal, Verano, Camaro, Cruze, Equinox, Malibu, Sonic, Volt, Terrain) the HVAC module logs it when both seat heaters quit: preliminary information PIC5954 blames intermittent software in seat heating module K29, which is reset by pulling its fuse for five minutes, and PIC5954B adds a reprogramming; replacin
s: Both front seat heaters inoperative
Side bolster adjustment of the driver seat does not react
c: Seat heating module software hangs (GM K29, reset and reprogram)
Stored history entry from a software anomaly (GM 2020–2023 SUVs)
Fuse or supply of the seat module
Seat harness damaged under the seat

U020A.d: U020A stands for moveable roof control module B, a second roof unit beside module A (U0207); which drive it controls, for instance a separate sunshade or a further glass panel, depends on the maker. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Second roof panel or sunshade does not move
Roof stops halfway or needs repeated button presses
c: Roof module software or missing initialisation
Wet or corroded connector in the headliner
Fuse or ground of roof module B

U020B.d: U020B is the last of the eight door module slots and flags lost contact with door control module H. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and on ordinary four-door cars the letter stays empty.
s: Window, lock or switches of one door inoperative
Door ajar or door system warning in the cluster
c: Poorly seated or corroded pins in the door-to-body connector
Wire break in the door transition

U020C.d: U020C means wireless accessory charging module A, the inductive Qi pad usually placed in the centre console, no longer talks on the network. No manufacturer documents this code publicly with module and threshold.
s: Phone does not charge on the wireless pad
No charging status shown on the centre display
c: Fuse or supply of the charging pad
Loose or damaged connector under the console

U020D.d: U020D is the second wireless charging slot, B, meant for vehicles with two inductive pads, for example a further one for rear passengers. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Second wireless pad does not charge, first still works
Charging indicator for that pad missing
c: Fuse or supply of charging pad B
Connector or harness to the second pad

U0210.d: U0210 flags lost contact with seat control module C. GM fills the slot in two ways: the 2011 Saab 9-5 list assigns it to the rear seat heating module, while bulletin 23-NA-206 and its predecessor PIT5762F (2020–2023 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Corvette, CT4, CT5) name the passenger front seat bladder control module, i.e.
s: Rear seat heating inoperative
Passenger lumbar support or massage does not react
Code stored only in history without any complaint
c: History entry from a software anomaly (GM 2020–2023, ignore if not current)
Fuse or supply of the seat module

U0211.d: U0211 reports that seat control module D is absent from the bus. GM bulletin 21-NA-131, which replaces PIT5796A (2020–2021 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon and 2021 Corvette, CT4, CT5), names it the memory seat module: the driver assistance controller EOCM records U0211 and invalid data U0512 when software in the memory seat module misbehaves.
s: Seat memory and easy entry/exit inoperative
Backrest will not recline fully
Driver assistance message or Super Cruise unavailable
c: Seat harness or connector under the driver seat

U0212.d: U0212 means the steering column control module, which reads stalks and steering wheel buttons such as wipers, turn signals and cruise switches, is missing from the network. Ford's 2023 diesel OBD summary lets the engine computer set it once the SCCM's message has been absent for more than 5 s, while the 2014 Ford list carries it with no MIL flag.
s: Wipers, turn signals or steering wheel buttons inoperative
Cruise control unavailable
Code stored in several modules without any complaint
c: False code mapping with electric column lock (GM N06, diagnose U0236)
Switch or airbag connectors at the column loose or corroded
Harness chafed at the base of the steering column

U0213.d: U0213 is set when mirror control module A stops reporting. In FCA vehicles A is the interior mirror: STAR case S2108000013 (2021 Jeep Grand Cherokee) found the BCM storing U0213-00 after a Restore Vehicle Configuration had wrongly marked the combined rear view mirror module CRVMM as fitted, for instance after enabling reverse camera grid lines per RRT 08-099-20; cars without that mirror then wait for messages that ne
s: Code active without any noticeable fault
Auto-dimming or camera display in the mirror inoperative
c: Mirror module enabled in configuration but not fitted (FCA)
Mirror connector at the windshield loose

U0214.d: U0214 stands for the remote function actuation module, the receiver for key fob, passive entry or phone as a key. Ford calls it RFA: SSM 51571 (Mustang Mach-E 2021–2023) and SSM 54773 (Nautilus 2021–2023) describe phone as a key failing and U0214 in several modules because the RFA hangs in programming mode following an over-the-air update; one minute without the RFA fuse in the BCM and a reprogramming bring it back.
s: Key fob, keyless entry or phone as a key inoperative
Intermittent no crank or radio and HVAC dropouts
c: RFA module stuck in programming mode after an update (Ford)
LAN wire to the receiver pinched in the headliner (GM Acadia)
Fuse or supply of the receiver module

U0215.d: U0215 is logged when door switch unit A, a keypad with its own small controller, stops answering on the bus. NXP application note AN2205 shows how such a keypad usually works: it is a LIN slave that never speaks unprompted; the body controller asks it roughly every 100 ms and expects a four-byte reply holding key states and LIN error flags.
s: Window, mirror or lock keys on one panel do nothing
Panel backlighting stays dark
Code returns after clearing, sometimes only when the door is moved
c: LIN or supply wire broken where the harness flexes at the door hinge
Switch unit A without battery feed or ground
LIN line shorted to ground or battery (often silences several nodes at once)
Electronics in switch unit A failed

U0216.d: U0216 reports that door switch unit B has dropped off the network. FCA uses the code on the 2014 Jeep Cherokee (KL) and its text names the driver door switch as the missing partner, so B is the driver's panel there.
s: Cluster message Start/Stop Not Available
Code appears after the battery was disconnected
Keys on the driver's switch panel may not respond
c: Vehicle configuration (Proxi) no longer consistent after battery disconnect
Damaged wiring or connector between driver door and body

U0217.d: U0217 is set when door switch unit C no longer answers its master. How much breaks then depends on the door architecture.
s: Other windows can no longer be operated from the driver's panel
Keys on the affected panel inoperative
Mirror adjustment from the panel unavailable
c: Broken wire in the flexing harness between door and body
Corroded or loose connector at the switch panel
Fault in the door or body module that polls the panel

U0218.d: U0218 means door switch unit D has gone silent. Rear-door panels are often bus nodes in their own right; on the 2011 Saab 9-5, GM even gives the left and right rear door switch panels separate codes.
s: Window key in one door has no effect
Same window still moves from the driver's panel
Rear window lockout behaves unexpectedly
c: Broken wire in the harness passage to the door
Moisture or corrosion at the switch panel connector
Body or door module not polling the panel correctly

U0219.d: U0219 means the networked door switch unit E is no longer heard. In modern doors the switch packs for windows, mirrors and locks are often small bus nodes, typically LIN slaves under a door or body module, so each panel can report its own communication loss.
s: Window, mirror or lock buttons in one door inoperative
Switch illumination off
Fault changes when the door is opened or closed
c: Broken wire in the door hinge area (flexing harness)
Water ingress into the door switch pack
Switch unit E without power or ground

U0220.d: U0220 reports that door switch unit F has stopped communicating. Water is a well-documented enemy of such units.
s: Window or lock keys work only intermittently
Window moves without a button press
Heat or burnt smell at the door switch panel
c: Water or salt slush inside the switch unit, corroded circuit board
Broken wire in the door harness
Switch unit failed without visible moisture

U0221.d: U0221 is stored when door switch unit G no longer replies. The weak spot is often the passage between door and body, where the harness bends at every opening.
s: Windows, locks and mirrors fail intermittently
Door-ajar warning while driving
Start/stop function stops working at times
c: Corroded door-to-body connector behind a poorly sealing grommet
Wire chafed or broken inside the grommet

U0222.d: U0222 says door window motor A, a motor with its own electronics, is no longer heard. GM uses it on 2021–2025 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon with air leveling (RPO F47): PIT5981B lists U0222 to U0225 as codes that can sit beside a low or leaning air suspension, a Service Leveling System message or short-term inflates that do nothing.
s: Air suspension low, leaning or not leveling
Service Leveling System message in the driver information center
Door shown as closed in scan data although it is open
Window in the affected door does not move
c: Door wiring altered or damaged during an upfit (armored car, limousine)
Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor A failed
Water or corrosion at the motor connector

U0223.d: U0223 points to door window motor B dropping out of communication; GM lists it in PIT5981B together with A, C and D for its 2021–2025 full-size SUVs. Smart motors keep learned data: Atmel's AVR480 reference stores blocking points and anti-pinch parameters in EEPROM and acquires them while the window is first operated.
s: Window in the affected door does not move at all
Express-up unavailable
Fault appears right after door panel or glass work
c: Motor or door connector not fully reconnected after door trim work
Broken wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor B failed
Blown fuse or missing ground for the motor

U0224.d: U0224 means door window motor C no longer reports in; GM's PIT5981B names it among the four window motor codes of its 2021–2025 full-size SUVs. Inside such a motor sits more than a driver stage: NXP's AN3147 reference counts Hall pulses to track glass position, detects pinching or stall and reports chip status such as overvoltage or overtemperature to the LIN master.
s: One-touch up and down unavailable
Window in the affected door does not move
Glass stops at random points or not at all
c: Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Motor electronics damaged (overvoltage, overheating, Hall sensor board)
Fuse or ground for motor C missing

U0225.d: U0225 marks door window motor D as missing from the bus. GM's PIT5981B names U0225 last in its list for 2021–2025 Escalade, Tahoe, Suburban and Yukon and notes that the cases came mainly from vehicles altered by upfitters, so door wiring touched during a conversion deserves the first look.
s: Window in the affected door inoperative
Air suspension not leveling on vehicles with door-ajar input via the motor
Further lost-communication codes from other door nodes
c: Door wiring changed during a vehicle conversion
LIN wire to motor D chafed, open or shorted
Electronics of window motor D failed

U0226.d: U0226 is stored when door window motor E stops answering. No manufacturer documents U0226 publicly, and the door behind letter E is the maker's choice.
s: Window stops working, often after rain or a car wash
Window moves jerkily before failing completely
Corrosion or moisture visible at the motor plug
c: Water inside the motor housing or its electronics
Door membrane or water deflector not sealing
Broken wire in the door harness

U0227.d: U0227 reports that door window motor F cannot be reached. Besides wiring faults, the LIN sleep and wake cycle is worth understanding here.
s: Window fails intermittently
Window and its one-touch function inoperative
c: Weak or interrupted supply or ground at the motor
LIN transceiver in the motor electronics damaged
Broken wire in the door harness
Software fault in the LIN master (door or body module)

U0228.d: U0228 concerns door window motor G, the last letter of this group. No manufacturer documents U0228 publicly.
s: Window in the affected door does not move
Pinch protection and one-touch operation unavailable
c: Broken bus or supply wire in the door harness
Electronics of window motor G failed

U0229.d: U0229 means the heated steering wheel module no longer answers. GM PIT5883G (December 2022) explains one harmless case: many 2022–2023 GM models were built during a parts shortage with the heated wheel disabled (RPO 00G); there U0229, together with U152B or U1530, may be stored, should be ignored and lights no warning.
s: Steering wheel heating does not switch on
Heater button indicator does not respond
Code stored without any noticeable fault (feature not fitted or disabled)
c: Heated wheel disabled from the factory (GM RPO 00G), code to be ignored
Module without fuse feed or ground
Clockspring interrupted (when the module sits in the steering wheel)
Heated steering wheel module failed or not configured

U022E.d: U022E reports that object detection maintenance control module A has stopped talking on the vehicle network. The J2012 name points to a unit that keeps the detection sensors of the driver assistance system usable, for example by washing or heating camera, radar or lidar covers; patent US11077472B2 describes such a cleaning device for an object detection sensor.
s: Sensor cleaning or sensor blocked warning
Driver assistance features unavailable
c: Module A without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Damaged or corroded bus wiring to module A
Washer fluid or water ingress at the module or its plug
Module A faulty or not programmed

U022F.d: U022F is the B counterpart: a control unit expects messages from object detection maintenance control module B and receives none. Cars with many cameras and radars could split sensor upkeep, such as washer pumps, nozzle valves or cover heaters, across two units, and B would then serve the second group; which sensors that is stays the maker's choice, because no manufacturer documents U022F publicly.
s: Sensor blocked or cleaning unavailable message
Camera or radar based assistance switched off
c: Fuse, ground or bus branch shared with module A interrupted
Module B faulty or software not matching

U0230.d: U0230 means the rear gate module, which runs a powered liftgate or tailgate with its drive, latch, cinch motor and pinch detection, has dropped off the bus. Toyota bulletin T-SB-0038-15 (Highlander and Highlander HV 2008-2013) names U0230 together with B2222 when the power back door reverses at the end of its travel or clunks at the striker, and gives a hinge and hatch inspection and repair.
s: Power liftgate does not open or close electrically
Gate reverses or stops during power closing
Several lost communication codes stored at once
c: Water or corrosion in the harness connector at the liftgate
Wires broken in the flexing harness between body and gate
Bus wiring chafed along the body (seat or pillar area)

U0231.d: U0231 shows that the rain sensing module on the windscreen, an optical unit that registers droplets and often ambient brightness too, no longer answers. It usually sits on a LIN line below a body or wiper controller, which stores the code.
s: Automatic wipers inoperative, manual stages still work
Automatic headlamps not switching
c: Sensor plug not seated after windscreen or mirror work
LIN wire damaged in the headliner or A-pillar

U0232.d: U0232 means side obstacle detection control module A, one of the rear corner radars for blind spot and cross traffic warning, is missing from the network. Saab's 2011 list puts A on the left; Toyota bulletin T-SB-0063-19 (Tacoma 2016-2018) calls U0232 loss of the blind spot slave module.
s: Blind spot system unavailable message
Mirror warning lamps do not light
Rear cross traffic alert inoperative
c: Mud, snow or ice packed between radar and bumper cover
Open fuse or pinched wiring in the rear body or liftgate

U0233.d: U0233 is stored when side obstacle detection control module B no longer reports. In the Saab 2011 list B is the right hand unit, which matches Volvo TJ 30858 (XC90, S90, 2016-2018): there the left sensor logs U023392 for the right one, and a software update is the fix.
s: Blind spot or cross traffic alert unavailable
Sensor blocked message without any obstacle
c: Dirt, snow or ice build-up behind the rear bumper

U0234.d: U0234 states that the convenience recall module has fallen silent on the network. Convenience recall means stored personal settings brought back on request or by key, typically seat, outside mirror, pedal and column positions and audio presets; patent US7525931B2 shows such a recall session started by a networked door module message.
s: Memory buttons for seat and mirrors without function
Driver profile not recalled with the key
c: Module without power or ground (fuse, connector under seat or door)
Harness under the seat pinched by seat travel

U0235.d: U0235 means the forward long range radar, the single or centre sensor that measures the gap to traffic ahead for adaptive cruise and collision warning, has gone quiet. GM's 2025 OBD summary 25OBDG04B lets the object calculation module EOCM3 set it when any of six radar data bursts is absent for more than 0.25 s at 9-16 V, skipped in transport mode, after resets and during bus-off; adaptive cruise is then disabled and
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Collision alert or driver assist unavailable message
c: Radar connector or wiring at the front end damaged (often after a collision)
Weak 12 V supply or BCM calibration (GM PIC6606)
Fault on the object or chassis bus shared with other modules

U0236.d: U0236 reports that the column lock module, which electrically bolts and frees the steering shaft as theft protection, has stopped communicating. It has nothing to do with the steering angle sensor (U0126).
s: Steering lock or service steering column warning
Engine does not crank or start
Steering wheel stays locked
c: Column lock module without power or ground (fuse, connector at column)
Harness at the steering column chafed or plug loose after column work
Low battery voltage during start request

U0237.d: U0237 means a third digital audio unit, module C, has gone silent. Ford uses the code in its newer infotainment layout: SSM 49737 (Mustang Mach-E 2021) and its follow-up SSM 51778 (2020-2022 Escape, Edge, Explorer, Expedition, F-150, Mach-E) list U0237 and U0238 when the speakers fall silent, chimes move to the instrument cluster and neither the ACM (audio control module) nor the digital signal processor (DSP) answer
s: No sound from the speakers
Warning chimes only from the instrument cluster
c: Audio DSP software hung or outdated (Ford SSM 49737/51778)

U0238.d: U0238 is set when digital audio control module D stops sending. In Ford and Lincoln vehicles this is the digital signal processor for audio that drives the amplified speaker set, and the code is mostly logged by the ACM, the audio control module.
s: Intermittent or permanent loss of audio
Premium sound system without output
c: DSP fuse open or with poor blade contact

U0239.d: U0239 means entrapment control module A no longer sends messages. Such a unit watches a power closing panel, a window, sunroof, sliding door or gate, for a trapped object and reverses the motor.
s: One-touch or automatic closing does not work
Window or sunroof needs re-initialisation
c: Module A without power or ground
Bus wire broken in door hinge or roof harness
Water in the module or plug (door, roof drain)

U023A.d: U023A reports loss of image processing module A, usually the windscreen camera feeding lane keeping, auto high beam and collision warning. Ford calls it IPMA: Mustang 2024 (SSM 52077) logs U023A in the SCCM after a remote start with Pre-Collision Assist unavailable, and F-150 2021-2023 (TSB 24-2267) shows U023A:08 after SCCM programming, fixed by IPMA software.
s: Service front camera or pre-collision assist unavailable message
Lane keeping and auto high beam off
Code only stored as history
c: Camera module software or low power mode handling (Ford IPMA)
History code logged at power down without real fault (GM PIC5814)
Instrument cluster swapped from a car without lane departure alert (Toyota)
Camera plug or wiring at the windscreen damaged

U023B.d: U023B points to image processing module B. GM uses it on its newer Super Cruise vehicles: PI PIC6607 (2026 Cadillac LYRIQ and VISTIQ) lists U023B SYM00 as a history entry next to U3000, U1624, U0140 and U053C and states that these do not explain a Super Cruise unavailable message, so the image processing module must not be replaced for them; the real fault is found with GM's Super Cruise diagnosis.
s: Super Cruise or camera based assistance unavailable
Surround view camera image blank
c: Power, ground or bus wiring to module B interrupted

U023C.d: U023C covers image processing module C, which GM uses for the video processing module (VPM) of its surround vision system. Bulletin 21-NA-209 (2021 Cadillac Escalade and Escalade ESV with RPO UXP) describes a black radio screen showing a triangle and a struck-through camera, with U023C and B1A62 current in the VPM K157; VPM software is the cause, and the repair is pulling fuse F28 for a minute, then reprogramming the
s: Black display with crossed-out camera symbol
Surround view cameras unavailable
Adaptive cruise control disabled
c: Fuse or supply to the video processing module
Camera or bus wiring to the module damaged

U023D.d: U023D means the left front distance range sensor, a short range corner radar that watches the area ahead and to the left of the bumper, has stopped reporting. Corner radars widen the field of view of the central long range radar, which helps adaptive cruise pick up cutting-in traffic.
s: Adaptive cruise control unavailable
Front cross traffic or collision assist limited
c: Connector or harness at the left front corner damaged (collision, bumper work)
Road salt corrosion at the radar plug

U023E.d: U023E is the mirror image for the right front corner: the short range radar on the passenger side of the front bumper no longer delivers its object data. Together with the left unit (U023D) and the centre long range radar (U0235) it gives adaptive cruise and collision assistance a wider view of vehicles merging into the lane.
s: Adaptive cruise control switched off
Driver assistance warning on the cluster
c: Right front corner radar wiring damaged after collision or bumper removal
Supply or bus fault shared with the left corner radar

U0240.d: U0240 flags the second anti-trap unit, entrapment control module B, as missing on the network. Where a vehicle has more than one automatically closing panel, for example a sunroof plus a power sliding door, each may carry its own reversal electronics, and B denotes one of them as assigned by the maker; no manufacturer documents U0240 publicly.
s: Automatic close function of a panel disabled
Panel only moves while the switch is held
c: Module B without power or ground
Wiring broken in a moving harness (sliding door, roof frame)

U0241.d: Headlamp control module A runs the electronic front lighting, for example beam levelling, cornering light or LED segments. Ford calls it HCM; it sits on the vehicle network and logs network faults of its own, as on the 2017 Lincoln MKZ after remote start (SSM 46508).
s: Headlamp or adaptive lighting warning in the cluster
Cornering, levelling or matrix functions inactive, basic low beam only
Several U codes in other modules at the same time
c: Headlamp module without power or ground (fuse, connector at the lamp)
Damaged or corroded bus wiring in the front end, often after a collision or lamp replacement
Network disturbed by another module or accessory staying awake (Land Rover cooler box)
Headlamp module software fault or internal failure

U0242.d: Many cars fit one control module per headlamp, and the second one carries letter B. Jaguar labels the pair HCMA and HCMB on the 2020 XE (SSM74402), Bentley addresses them as light control left and right on the Continental GT (campaign 2056293/1), and a 2024 scan-tool release lists an HCMB for the Land Rover Discovery Sport.
s: Lighting warning in the cluster
Headlamp on one side without adaptive or LED functions
Daytime running or position light out on one side
c: Module B without power or ground, e.g. blown fuse or loose lamp connector
Fault in a fuse, ground or bus branch shared with module A
Headlamp replaced without programming or with mismatched software

U0243.d: Parking assist module B is a second parking controller beside the main one, which J2012 covers with U0159. Stellantis uses the code by name: on 2021–2023 Jeep Grand Cherokee and 2022–2023 Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer the cluster and the module listed as ETM store U0243-00 for lost contact with the central vision park assist module (CVPAM), which handles the surround view cameras, while body, steering and blind spot mo
s: Blue or blank screen in surround, front or rear camera view
Parking aid unavailable message
U0159 stored in several other modules at the same time
c: Camera/park module hung by software, recovers after a power reset or update
Module B without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged or corroded

U0244.d: Power running boards fold out when a door opens and stow when doors close or the vehicle starts moving; Ford's running board control module (RBM) runs the motors. Ford documents U0244 directly: on 2027 Expedition and Navigator the boards intermittently refuse to move and the cluster shows a running board fault message; the driver seat module (DSM) holds C1008:15 or C1009:15 while other modules record U0208 and U0244.
s: Power running board fault message in the cluster
Boards stay extended or retracted
Seat heating, cooling or memory affected at the same time (Ford 2027)
c: Software fault in the module hosting the running board function (Ford 2027: driver seat module)
Low or fully discharged battery that left the module offline
Damaged or corroded wiring and connectors exposed under the body

U0245.d: The front entertainment module is the head unit with radio, navigation and the central display. Mitsubishi uses U0245 for this unit and spells out the logic: in its workshop manuals the combination meter sets the code when, with ignition on, 10–16 V and an intact supply fuse, it receives nothing from the audio visual navigation unit for 2,500 ms; a 2019 manual has the camera ECU apply the same 2,500 ms limit to the m
s: Radio and central display dark or frozen
Rear camera image or climate display on the screen missing
U0245 stored in several modules at once
c: Head unit rebooting or being updated, code left behind as history (erase afterwards)
Head unit without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the dash)
CAN wiring or connector between head unit and receiving module faulty

U0246.d: Seat control module E belongs to the letters beyond driver and passenger units. Ford fills it with the front seat climate control module (SCME), which runs heating and the backrest and cushion fans of the front seats; its 2024 module list in a scan-tool release names SCME that way.
s: Front seat heating and ventilation inoperative
Seat climate buttons or touchscreen entries without response
c: Loose, pinched or corroded connector under the front seat
Climate seat module without power or ground (fuse)
Module replaced or updated without correct configuration

U0247.d: In Ford's module naming, letter F stands for the rear seat climate control module (SCMF), the unit that heats and, where fitted, ventilates the second-row outboard seats; a 2024 scan-tool release lists it next to SCME for the front seats and SCMG/SCMH for the multi-contour seats. Ford's climate seat bulletins show how such a unit is serviced: stored codes are read in the module first, then blower or configuration are
s: Rear seat heating or ventilation inoperative
Rear seat climate buttons without response
c: Harness or connector strained by folding or sliding the second-row seat
Rear climate seat module without power or ground
Module internally faulty, for example after liquid spilled on the seat

U0248.d: No manufacturer explains publicly what the remote accessory module does or when U0248 is set. The name suggests a body-side unit that switches accessories outside the main controllers.
s: Accessory function controlled by the module inoperative
Code stored in other modules without noticeable fault
c: Module without power or ground (fuse, connector)
Retrofitted or removed accessory, module configured but not present
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged

U0249.d: Rear B is the second rear entertainment unit; GM applies the code to a concrete part. Its 2011 Saab 9-5 code list names U0249 as lost communication with the rear radio audio control module, the rear seat audio controls with their own headphone outputs.
s: Rear audio controls or headphone outputs dead
Second rear screen without picture
Many U codes across modules, radio may switch off while driving
c: Chafed or burnt network wiring elsewhere in the vehicle (GM: harness on muffler)
Rear unit without power or ground
Loose or corroded connector at the rear unit

U024A.d: Interior lighting control module A switches and dims cabin lights such as dome, footwell and ambient strips. In newer cars these are often small LIN nodes under a master, usually the body controller.
s: Interior lights do not come on or stay on
Ambient lighting colour or brightness cannot be changed
c: Loose or corroded plug at a roof, door or footwell light unit
LIN line chafed or pinched in headliner, door or trim
Lighting module without power or ground

U024B.d: Ford assigns seat control module G to the driver's multi-contour seat (SCMG), which runs massage and lumbar adjustment. Two Ford bulletins name U024B.
s: Driver seat massage and lumbar inoperative or intermittent
Seat settings on the SYNC screen without response
B1471 stored alongside
c: Fretting corrosion in the SCMG connector terminals under the seat
Module misconfigured after a software update (configuration app not run)
Seat harness strained by seat travel or poor routing

U024C.d: Seat control module H is Ford's passenger multi-contour seat module (SCMH), the mirror of the driver unit G. It shares the fretting connector problem of TSB 19-2293: on the listed Ford and Lincoln vehicles passenger massage and lumbar act up, sometimes with U024C stored, and the repair replaces the SCMH connector and reroutes the harness.
s: Passenger seat massage or lumbar inoperative or intermittent
Passenger seat functions unavailable on the SYNC screen
c: Fretting corrosion in the SCMH connector terminals
SCMH misconfigured after a software update
Passenger seat harness strained by seat movement

U024D.d: Ford uses seat control module J (SCMJ), also called power fold seat module (PFSM), for the electrically folding third row. On 2025 Expedition and Navigator a software fault made the seats ignore the 3L, Both and 3R buttons; a relearn with the engine running and the liftgate open, holding Both for one minute and five seconds more after the seats stop, restores them until an update arrives (SSM 53681).
s: Third-row power fold buttons without effect
Seats stop half-way or stand misaligned
c: Harness or connector damaged where it flexes with the folding seat
Fold seat module without power or ground (fuse)
Module software locked up, needs relearn or update

U024E.d: Side obstacle detection modules are radar units that watch the blind spots and crossing traffic. Left and right units have their own codes, U0232 and U0233; letters C and D cover extra units.
s: Blind spot system unavailable message
Blind spot and cross-traffic alerts missing
c: Radar connector or harness in the bumper damaged, wet or corroded
Replacement or used module not configured for the vehicle
Radar module without power or ground

U024F.d: Module D is the fourth side radar in Ford's scheme beside SODL, SODR and SODCMC. Ford's bulletins list SODCMD among units that log U2100 or U3002 after replacement on 2021–2025 models; SSM 53569 adds that a VIN mismatch can also follow swapping a tail lamp from another car, and that radar modules cannot move between vehicles without programming.
s: Side assist or blind spot warning message
One monitoring zone without alerts
c: Rear radar harness chafed or heat-damaged near exhaust or bumper
Module or tail lamp from another vehicle fitted without programming
Radar module without power or ground

U0250.d: Within the airbag system, an impact classification module sorts a collision by type and force, so that airbags and belt pretensioners fire in the right combination and stage. U0250 is logged when its messages no longer reach the network, most plausibly by the restraint control module.
s: Airbag warning lamp on
Code also stored in the restraint control module
c: Loose or corroded connector or damaged harness to the module, often after body repair
Module damaged in a collision or not set up after replacement

U0251.d: Letter B denotes a second running board controller, which only exists where each side has its own unit. Ford's documented power running boards rely on a single running board control module (RBM): its 2015–2022 bulletins describe one RBM that logs U3003:16 and turns the feature from Auto to Off after a low or flat battery (SSM 50154) and one whose software flips the setting on F-Super Duty (SSM 52411).
s: Running board on one side does not deploy or retract
Running board fault message in the cluster
c: Water or salt corrosion at underbody connectors and wiring
Low or flat battery that left the module offline

U0252.d: Module B for rear lighting is the second unit driving lamps at the back end, and in practice it is often the trailer electronics. GM's code list for the 2011 Saab 9-5 assigns U0252 to the trailer interface control module.
s: Trailer brake module fault or trailer warning in the cluster
Trailer lamps or rear lighting functions inoperative
Further U codes such as U0137 in body control module, cluster or steering module
c: Trailer or rear lighting module stuck off the bus, software needs reset or update (Ford TRM)
Loose or badly tightened body ground shared with the module (Ford G201)
Damaged or corroded harness and connectors at the rear or tow bar area
Stored history entry from a module self-test without a real fault

U0253.d: The accessory protocol interface module is Ford's SYNC computer (APIM), which connects touchscreen, phone and voice functions with the vehicle network. Other modules log U0253 when its frames stop arriving, and Ford bulletins show several listeners: the headlamp module of the 2017 Lincoln MKZ after a remote start, cured by new HCM software (SSM 46508); the FCIM switch panel of 2015-2017 F-150 trucks, which froze unde
s: Center screen dark, frozen or rebooting
Drive mode or settings fall back to default, message Drive Mode Not Available
Code stored in ABS, headlamp or switch module without noticeable fault
c: APIM or receiving-module software fault, fixed by reprogramming or over-the-air update
APIM without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the center display)
Network overload or a module locking up after remote start or battery work
Internal failure of the SYNC module

U0254.d: A remote start module runs the engine from a key fob or app so the cabin can be heated or cooled before departure. GM's list for the 2011 Saab 9-5 treats it as a network node of its own under U0254.
s: Remote start does not work or stops after a short time
Code found only during a full system scan, no other complaint
c: Software interface mismatch between gateway and accessory starter (Subaru), no real fault
Poor installation, loose connector or missing supply of an accessory or aftermarket starter
Starter removed or disconnected while the vehicle configuration still expects it
Internal failure of the remote start module

U0255.d: The front display interface module is the central screen in the dashboard. Ford calls it FDIM; in the U-code table of the 2011 Saab 9-5, a GM design, the same node is the info display module with U0255.
s: Central screen black or frozen
Audio, climate or vehicle settings cannot be shown or changed
With gateway faults also dead gauges, warning messages or no crank
c: Gateway module locked up or its connector terminals loose, many U codes at once (GM SDGM)
Display without power or ground (fuse, connector behind the screen)
Damaged bus wiring to the display after dashboard work
Internal failure of the display module

U0256.d: Module A of the front controls interface collects radio and climate key presses in the middle of the dash and passes them to the network. At Ford this is the FCIM; for the 2011 Saab 9-5 GM labels U0256 as the infotainment faceplate control module.
s: Radio and climate keys on the center panel without function
Several warning lamps or messages at once, intermittent operation
Code only as history entry in the body controller, no complaint
c: Panel locked up by heavy network traffic, cleared by battery reset or new software
History entry left by a body controller self-test without a real fault (Ford :87)
Loose connector or missing supply at the panel after dashboard work
Internal failure of the control panel

U0257.d: Some vehicles combine keys and screen in a single front controls/display interface module. Ford calls such a unit FCDIM, for example with the small audio display on the Escape (2013-2016) and the 2016 Transit Connect, Transit and Focus (SSM 47234), while the 2011 Saab 9-5 reserves U0257 for a unit merging info display and faceplate.
s: Screen does not respond to touch or stays dark
Radio preset or menu keys without function or erratic
c: Software fault in the combined display unit (Audi panoramic display)
Unit without power or ground, or connector not fully seated after dashboard work
Internal failure of the combined controls/display unit
Fault on the infotainment bus branch shared with other units

U0258.d: Despite its name this unit has nothing to do with the audio tuner: Ford's radio transceiver module (RTM) handles the wireless link to keys and remote accessories. On the 2021-2022 Bronco Sport, Ford traced No Key Detected messages to blocked key frequencies or a flat key battery and advised laying the key in the forward console tray, the backup position close to the RTM (SSM 50341); RTMs in recent F-150 and Super Dut
s: No Key Detected or key not recognized at start-up
Keyless entry, remote locking or keypad without function
c: Transceiver without power or ground, or loose connector
Open or shorted data line between transceiver and its master module
Transceiver software or configuration not matching after replacement
Internal failure of the radio transceiver

U0259.d: A special purpose vehicle control module is extra electronics for converted vehicles such as police cars, ambulances or work trucks. GM sells one from 2024 as Universal Vehicle Module (option KGU) and calls it special purpose vehicle control module for Silverado and Sierra pickups and the Tahoe and Blazer EV police vehicles.
s: Light bar, siren or other conversion functions inoperative or stuck
Upfitter switches or configurable inputs without effect
c: Add-on controller without power or ground from the body builder's circuits
Damaged or wrongly spliced bus wiring from the conversion
Retrofit without the required vehicle configuration and module programming
Internal failure of the special purpose controller

U025A.d: U025A concerns the second slot for special purpose controllers. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Functions of the second conversion unit inoperative
Warning or message from the conversion control panel
c: Second add-on unit unpowered, often via a switched or separately fused upfit circuit
Faulty splice or connector where the conversion joins the vehicle bus
Unit removed or replaced while the vehicle still expects it

U025B.d: With U025B a module on the bus reports that controller C (third slot of four) has gone quiet. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Conversion functions of unit C inoperative
Programming or configuration tool cannot reach the unit
c: Software of vehicle modules and add-on unit not at matching levels
Controller C without power or ground from the upfit circuits
Fault on the sub-bus or link through which the unit is attached

U025C.d: U025C is the last of the four lost-communication codes for special purpose controllers and covers unit D. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and none of the published systems names more than one such controller.
s: Functions of the fourth conversion unit inoperative
Code stored without any noticeable complaint
c: Vehicle configuration lists a fourth add-on unit that is not fitted or was removed
Unit D without power, ground or bus connection

U025D.d: Front controls interface module B is a second switch panel at the front where the controls are split over two units. Ford uses this name (FCIMB): on 2023 Transit vans having SYNC 3 Lite and parking aid at the rear only, the parking aid disable switch sits in that panel, and vans built between 15 March and 2 June 2023 ignored it, since the park aid module carried a wrong configuration (SSM 51837).
s: Switches on the second front panel without function
Functions that rely on head unit data unavailable (Mercedes)
c: Second panel without power or ground, or connector loose after dashboard work
Head unit not on the bus where the maker maps U025D to it (Mercedes)
Wrong configuration of the panel or of the module that uses its switches
Internal failure of the second control panel

U025E.d: Instead of a vacuum servo, an electronic brake booster uses a pedal travel sensor and an electric motor for the assist, which also lets regenerative braking be blended in, as in Bosch's iBooster. Mitsubishi documents U025E-00 in the engine control module of the Outlander PHEV from 2023, where it means lost contact with the EBA, the electric driven intelligent brake unit.
s: Check engine lamp after repeated detection (Mitsubishi)
Brake, ABS or stability warning lamps on
Harder brake pedal or reduced regenerative braking
c: Damaged CAN wiring or connector between engine or brake controllers and the booster unit
Fault in the booster's power supply (high-current fuse, ground, 12 V battery)
Internal failure of the electric brake unit
Failure of the receiving engine control module

U025F.d: U025F concerns a second electronic brake booster control unit, B. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none states which physical unit would carry the letter.
s: Brake system or driver-assist warning in the cluster
Automated or assisted driving functions unavailable
c: Second brake unit without power or ground (separate fuse or supply path)
Damaged bus wiring or connector to the redundant unit
Internal failure of brake unit B

U0260.d: Many power seat switches now contain electronics that scan the keys and report the result over a LIN or multiplex link rather than carrying motor current. A Lear patent describes a seat motor assembly with integrated electronics that talks to an external switch over a one- or two-wire multiplex link.
s: Seat cannot be adjusted with its switch
Memory, lumbar or massage keys on that switch without function
c: Switch module software stuck in sleep mode, reset by unplugging and fixed by update
Loose or corroded connector or broken wire at the switch in the door or seat trim
LIN line to the seat module shorted or open
Internal failure of the switch module

U0261.d: Seat control switch module B is a further switch unit with its own electronics, serving another seat or seat row; which position the letter stands for is not published. Lincoln bulletins show how closely switch and seat module interact: power seats in the second row of the 2025 Navigator did not slide when the switch was pressed, the rear seat modules SCMK/SCML held B167F:11, and the cure was to run their configurati
s: Passenger or rear seat does not move with its switch
Seat settings missing in the center display
c: Seat module configuration or software not matching the switch (Lincoln SCMK/SCML)
Loose connector or chafed wire under the seat or in the trim of the second switch
Wrong part level of the seat switch after production or replacement
Internal failure of switch module B

U0262.d: Large sound systems may use a second external amplifier, audio amplifier B. Such amplifiers take part in network traffic: a patent on modular add-on sound systems explains that the factory amplifier decodes gain commands that the head unit sends over the CAN bus, and that a replacement amplifier must therefore understand the maker's bus format, such as GMLAN.
s: Some speakers silent while others still play
Static, crackling or sound dropping out
c: Amplifier connector not locked or pushed back, often in the rear harness
Amplifier B without power or ground (own fuse, switched supply)
Aftermarket audio installation that removed or bypassed the second amplifier

U0263.d: A speech recognition module turns spoken commands into actions for phone, audio or navigation. Some makers place it in a separate box: FCA built Uconnect Voice Command into its hands-free unit (HFM) of 2012-2017 Journey, Charger and 300.
s: No reaction to the voice button on the steering wheel
Message that speech recognition cannot be started
Hands-free phone functions unavailable where combined in one module
c: Voice module software hangs during start-up, fixed by reflash
Voice module without power or ground, or connector loose
Fault message created by cluster or head unit software although the module works
Internal failure of the speech recognition module

U0264.d: The rear camera module supplies the reversing picture; whichever unit expects its messages stores U0264 when they stop, depending on the brand the radio, the body controller, the cluster or a central vision module. FCA uses it widely: a 2021 Ram 1500 logged it in the radio after connector XY552A worked loose once the tailgate had been off (S2108000050), and 2019–2020 Ram heavy-duty trucks with surround view set it in
s: Black or blank screen when reverse is selected
Camera system fault message, surround view button greyed out
Code stored in radio, cluster or body controller, sometimes with blind spot faults
c: Camera connector in tailgate or liftgate loose or not fully seated, often after body work
Pinched or chafed wire in the liftgate, camera fuse blown
New camera paired with outdated software in the display or vision module
Rear camera or camera control module internally faulty

U0265.d: GM gives sensor A a clear identity: its bulletins describe U0265 as lost contact with the front view camera on the windshield (B174W), the camera for forward collision alert and steering assistance. On 2020 Cadillac CT4 and CT5 with forward collision alert that camera could reset itself; U0265 then came with U0566, U1962 and P25A2, a brake module request that can switch on the MIL, plus Service Driver Assist and Stee
s: Service Driver Assist or front camera message, lane and collision functions unavailable
Steering assist reduced message on some models
Emergency braking lamp briefly amber, then normal again
c: Windshield camera resets or drops off the bus because of its software
Camera hardware fault when the loss recurs often and is easy to repeat
Connector or supply at the camera mount disturbed, e.g. after windshield work
Fault on the shared bus that silences several sensors at once

U0266.d: Image processing sensor B has a documented owner at FCA, which reads U0266-00 as lost communication with the left camera of its 360-degree surround view. The central vision processing module (CVPM) takes each camera on its own colour-coded coaxial plug.
s: Left side of the surround or top view black, other views normal
Fault appears intermittently, often after door work
Left camera performance code stored as well
c: Coaxial camera lead in the driver door harness damaged or unplugged
Door or kick panel connector not secured after door repair
Camera plug loose at the central vision processing module

U0267.d: No vehicle maker documents U0267 in public service material, so the camera behind letter C remains unknown, and letters are assigned differently from brand to brand. What can break is clear from the hardware.
s: One camera view or camera-based assistant unavailable
Service message for the camera or driver assistance
c: Camera link cable open or shorted, connector corroded
Link loses lock due to bit errors from a degraded cable or interference
Sensor C without supply, for example power over the coaxial line missing

U0268.d: GM files U0268 among the codes of its object detection bus, a separate network that links the active safety module with the radars and the front camera on Cadillac Escalades of model years 2015–2020 equipped with driver assistance. Which sensor letter D denotes is not stated in the bulletins.
s: Service messages for surround camera, park assist and adaptive cruise
Front parking, turn, daytime or cornering lamps dead, turn signal flashes fast
Several radar and camera U-codes stored at once
c: Front fascia harness chafed at the right bumper bar, fuses blown
Connector of sensor D loose or damaged after front-end repairs
Short or open on the object detection bus

U0269.d: U0269 is a further member of GM's object detection group, kept by the active safety module first on 2015 Escalades with the Y66 driver assist package and, after a 2017 update, on many 2013–2018 Buick, Cadillac and Chevrolet models; GM does not publish which sensor letter E names. Its known trap is in the workshop: that bus uses its own circuits 3813 and 3811, which run to terminal 3 and terminal 11 of the DLC, which
s: Scan tool cannot reach radars or front camera, several U-codes at once
Service Active Safety, Service Driver Assist or lane departure message
Code present only while a particular tester is connected
c: Defective scan tool interface or cable on the object detection pins, false code
Object detection bus wiring damaged, for example in the front fascia
Sensor E without power or ground

U026A.d: At GM letter F belongs to the frontview camera module (K109, later B174W) on the windshield, which serves forward collision alert, IntelliBeam and the lane departure and lane keeping functions. On 2016–2017 Chevrolet, GMC and Cadillac models such as Malibu, Silverado, Tahoe and Escalade, early camera software made the cluster or body module store a history U026A or U023A while the Service Front Camera message came an
s: Intermittent Service Front Camera message
Lane departure warning, lane keep assist, collision alert or automatic high beam inoperative
Weak battery after standing for days, camera warm with ignition off
c: Camera software sets false history codes or locks up, cured by reprogramming
Pushed-in or missing terminals in the camera connector
Supply or bus wiring to the windshield camera interrupted

U026B.d: Letter G, too, is visible only through GM: U026B appears in the active safety controller of Escalades from 2015 fitted with the Y66 assistance package, always grouped with U0265, U0268, U0269, U026A, U026C and U0075, and GM does not say which radar or camera G is. The grouping is itself the diagnostic hint.
s: Driver assistance or object detection service message
Code alone or together with U0075 and other sensor codes
c: Common cause on the object detection bus or its supply when several codes appear
Plug or fuse of sensor G when the code appears alone
Faulty scan tool cable producing false codes

U026C.d: U026C rounds off the GM object detection group reported by the Escalade's active safety module; GM leaves open which sensor letter H stands for. The PIT5487 series, revised from 2016 up to version F in 2020 for model years 2015–2020, shows how the code turns up next to lighting faults.
s: Turn signal flashes fast, front lamps partly dead
Lamp body codes stored together with sensor U-codes
Service Driver Assist or surround camera message
c: Chafed bumper harness supplying both lamps and sensors
Shared fuse blown by a short in the front wiring
Connector of sensor H loose or corroded

U026D.d: No manufacturer documents U026D publicly, and the camera filed under letter I is unknown. Among the image sensors that now sit on the bus as modules of their own is the driver-facing camera: Ford runs a driver status monitor camera module (CMR) on the 2021 Mustang Mach-E and later on F-150, Expedition, Navigator and Corsair.
s: Camera-based function unavailable with a service message
Sensor not reachable in the module scan
c: Wiring or connector to sensor I interrupted
Sensor I without supply or ground
Sensor I not responding because of software or configuration

U026E.d: U026E is not documented publicly by any manufacturer, so it is not known which camera letter J denotes. Exposed outside cameras show where such links are vulnerable.
s: One camera image black or frozen
Fault more frequent in rain or after washing
c: Water in an exposed camera housing or plug, corroded contacts
Camera lead damaged at a hinge, mirror arm or body passage

U026F.d: Neither U026F nor the meaning of letter K appears in published manufacturer material. Some image sources are optional or arrive with towing equipment, and that matters before diagnosing a silent camera.
s: Extra camera view missing or greyed out
View works only with or only without a trailer connected
c: Camera function expected although the vehicle lacks the option or configuration
Plug connection of an add-on or trailer camera open or corroded
Display or radio software not handling the camera input

U0270.d: U0270 ends the image sensor series, and no vehicle maker documents it publicly, so the camera behind letter L is unknown. Twelve letters reflect how many image sensors a vehicle can carry, and they compete for a limited number of receiver inputs: Texas Instruments' DS90UB954 hub, for example, combines one or two camera or radar links.
s: Function of sensor L unavailable with a service message
Fault right after retrofitting or replacing a camera
c: Sensor fitted or retrofitted without matching configuration, or configured but absent
Link cable or connector to sensor L interrupted

U0271.d: Seat control switch module C is a third switch unit with its own electronics that reports key presses to a seat module instead of carrying motor current. No manufacturer documents U0271 publicly, and which seat C serves is unpublished.
s: Seat does not move from this switch, other controls normal
Memory or comfort keys of this seat without function
c: Spread or loose terminals in the switch connector
Signal wire between switch and seat module chafed under the seat or in the door
Switch module C without supply or ground

U0272.d: Seat control switch module D is the fourth switch unit in this series; no manufacturer documents U0272 publicly or says which seat it belongs to. Such switches need not sit on the seat at all.
s: Rear or folding seat does not respond to its switch
Seat stops short of its end position
c: Wiring to a switch mounted away from the seat (console, roof, trim) interrupted
Seat module lost its learned positions or needs new calibration
Switch module D without supply or ground

U0273.d: A lighting driver control module sits in or on a headlamp and powers its LED groups on command from a higher-level lamp or body controller. U0273 means that controller hears nothing from driver module A within its timeout.
s: Lighting warning in the instrument cluster
Adaptive high beam, cornering light or light animation unavailable
LED segments on one headlamp dark or in a default setting
c: Moisture or corrosion at the headlamp connector of driver module A
Driver module A without supply or ground (fuse, splice)
Module software outdated or update interrupted
Driver module A internally faulty (often only with complete headlamp)

U0274.d: U0274 is stored when the second lighting driver control module stops answering on its network. Lincoln documents a B unit on the 2025 Navigator, listed as LDCMB and updated with the same release 25.10.08 as its three siblings, but gives no position for it.
s: Lamp stays at one fixed brightness and ignores dimming
Lighting fault message
Adaptive light functions switched off
c: Bus wire or connector to driver module B open or corroded
Supply or ground of driver module B missing
Driver module B software not current after an update

U0275.d: Driver module C is the third LED driver unit a lamp controller can address. Three or more of them appear where each headlamp has several separately driven zones, as on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, whose release notes name LDCMC alongside A, B and D.
s: Part of the headlamp light pattern missing or static
Warning for lighting system
c: Lamp harness or connector to module C damaged (e.g. after front-end repair)
Power or ground of module C interrupted
Module C internally faulty or overheated

U0276.d: U0276 closes the four-letter block: the controlling module has lost contact with lighting driver control module D. Lincoln names an LDCMD on the 2025 Navigator and updated it in the same over-the-air package as A to C; nothing more about its location is public, and no manufacturer documents U0276.
s: Automatic or adaptive high beam deactivated, manual switching still works
Lighting warning in the cluster
c: Connector of module D loose, wet or corroded
Bus line to module D chafed or open

U0277.d: Ford uses seat control module K for a second-row seat: on the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, SCMK drives the power seat behind the driver, in SSM 54226 called the rear left-hand power seat module. Its update SCMK-25.5.5.3 was meant to make that seat store its memory positions reliably, and SSM 54226 deals with second-row seats stuck in their longitudinal position, B167F:11 stored in SCMK or SCML, which moved again only afte
s: Left second-row power seat does not move
Memory positions of that seat not stored or recalled
c: Seat harness or connector under the second-row seat strained or unplugged
SCMK not configured or software update incomplete
Seat module fuse or supply open
Seat control module K internally faulty

U0278.d: Seat control module L is the right-hand partner of K. On the 2025 Lincoln Navigator, Ford's SCML runs the second-row power seat on the passenger side; release SCML-25.5.5.3 targeted its memory function, and SSM 54226 lists it as the rear right-hand power seat module, with its own configuration app that must be run after a module change, for example when the seat ignores its fore-aft switch.
s: Right second-row power seat inoperative
Seat memory on that seat not working
c: Harness under the sliding seat damaged by seat movement
SCML configuration missing after replacement or update
Power or ground to SCML interrupted
Seat control module L internally faulty

U0279.d: A haptic control module produces vibrations or pulses that the occupants feel, for example in the steering wheel, a seat or the floor. Where it sits varies: the 2026 Range Rover has separate haptic floor modules under the carpet, while on the 2019–2022 Hyundai Palisade the haptic steering wheel motor is driven by the integrated central control unit, so there is no separate network node.
s: No vibration warning in steering wheel, seat or floor
Message about haptic or warning system in the cluster
c: Connector of the haptic module loose, e.g. after seat or carpet removal
Supply or ground of the haptic module interrupted
Vehicle configured for a haptic option the module does not match

U027A.d: Module C is a third on-board charger in the same vehicle; A and B have U019B and U01BB. Several chargers on one bus need clearly separated roles, and a Lear patent shows one way: each unit reads a coded input at start-up, then joins the vehicle bus either as master with the master message set or as slave with the slave set.
s: Reduced AC charging power or longer charging time
Charging fault message
c: 12 V supply or wake-up line of charger C missing
Bus connector at charger C corroded or not latched
Charger C coded or addressed wrongly after replacement

U027B.d: U027B refers to a fourth charger unit. In multi-charger designs the units also split the control task; in a dual charger system patented by Lear, two chargers feed the battery in parallel, one regulating voltage and the other regulating current.
s: Charging power lower than usual
Charging session aborted with a warning
c: Low-voltage supply, fuse or wake-up of charger D missing
Bus wiring to charger D damaged or connector wet

U027C.d: DC fast charging uses a charger outside the car, so the vehicle needs a controller that negotiates with the station. Ford has a module with almost this name in its battery-electric vehicles: the off-board charger controller (OBCC) of the Mustang Mach-E, E-Transit and F-150 Lightning.
s: DC fast charging fails or does not start
Charge failure notification on screen or in the app
AC charging still possible
c: Supply or wake-up of the fast-charge controller missing
Controller software outdated or update failed
Bus wiring or connector to the controller faulty

U0284.d: The grille shutter actuator is a LIN node of the engine controller. GM's 2018 ECM tables set U0284 when the ECM loses the LIN link to shutter 1 for 3 counts in Run with at least 11 V; it is Type B, MIL after two trips.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Grille shutter warning, shutters do not open or close
Check charging system message when a shared connection is affected
c: Water intrusion and corrosion at the shutter actuator connector or its harness
Fault on a shared connection, e.g. with the generator (check U012D/U042E)
Unstable power supply to the actuator
Shutter actuator A internally faulty or damaged by impact

U0285.d: Module B is the second shutter unit, typically the one behind the lower bumper opening. GM's 2018 ECM tables treat it as LIN device 1 (shutter 2): the ECM sets U0285 after 3 missed counts once the check has been enabled for 400 ms in Run at 11 V or more, Type B with MIL after two trips.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on, often with P05AE
Lower grille shutters do not move
Active air flap warning message
c: Corrosion in the lower shutter harness or connector from water and salt
Lower shutter or its wiring damaged by impact or debris

U0286.d: Some low-emission vehicles carry a catalytic radiator coating that breaks down ground-level ozone; BASF sells it as PremAir, and EPA and CARB grant 5 mg/mi credit for it. CARB requires the OBD system to watch such a direct ozone reduction system.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Further codes for the ozone reduction system or radiator temperature
c: Connector or wiring of the device at the radiator corroded or damaged
Radiator replaced and device missing or broken off

U0287.d: An electric transmission fluid pump with its own control electronics keeps hydraulic pressure available whenever the engine stands still, in auto stop or electric driving. Stellantis calls it transmission fluid pump module 1; the TCM sets U0287 when it stops responding.
s: Malfunction indicator lamp and service transmission or hybrid message
Engine stop-start disabled
Limp mode on plug-in hybrids
c: Electric fluid pump or its integrated electronics failed
Damaged high-voltage cable inducing interference on the pump circuit (hybrids)

U0288.d: A DC/AC converter, usually called a power inverter, turns the vehicle's direct current into 120 V or 230 V alternating current for sockets in the cabin or the load bed. U0288 is logged when the module supervising those sockets stops receiving the cyclic frames of converter A.
s: 120 V or 230 V outlets without power
Outlet or power supply warning in the instrument cluster
Code stored without any noticeable symptom
c: Body or gateway module configured for an outlet the vehicle does not have (false entry)
Outdated software in the converter or inverter system controller
Blown fuse, supply or bus wiring fault at converter A

U0289.d: U0289 belongs to a second DC/AC converter, unit B, in vehicles that generate mains-voltage alternating current at two points, for example a small inverter for a console socket and a stronger one for the bed, or one converter per group of outlets. No manufacturer documents U0289 or describes a converter B in public material.
s: Some outlets dead while others still work
Power outlet warning message
c: Network configured for a second converter that is missing or not activated
No supply or ground at converter B (fuse, connector)
Bus wiring or connector to converter B damaged

U028A.d: An electric transmission fluid pump with built-in electronics holds clutch pressure and lubrication whenever the engine is stopped, in auto stop or electric driving. Module B is a second pump of this kind; U028A means the transmission or hybrid controller no longer hears its status frames.
s: Start-stop function no longer active
Electric driving blocked or engine keeps running
Transmission warning, harsh engagement after an engine stop
c: Electric pump B or its integrated electronics failed
Corroded or loose pump connector, oil wicking into the connector
Supply, ground or bus line to pump B interrupted

U028B.d: Shutter module C is a third, separately addressed flap actuator behind the grille or bumper, used where a front end divides its cooling air openings into several sections. Hyundai documents the code: its 2026 Palisade and Palisade Hybrid have left and right actuators for the lower active air flaps, and campaign 26-01-026H lists U028B together with U0285 and flap position codes when water enters the bumper connectors
s: Check engine lamp on
Active air flap warning in the cluster
Lower flaps no longer move
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the bumper connector of shutter C
Front harness damaged by impact, stone chips or poor routing
Fault in the controlling engine module or its LIN output

U028C.d: Module D is the fourth grille shutter address in the code list and only matters on fronts with four independently driven flap units, for instance upper and lower flaps on each side. No manufacturer documents U028C or says where unit D sits, so its position is maker-specific.
s: Check engine lamp on
Part of the shutters stays open or closed
Slightly longer warm-up or higher consumption
c: Moisture or corrosion at the connector of shutter D
LIN or supply wire to unit D damaged in the front end
Actuator D failed, for example after ice or impact
Wrong actuator variant or configuration after a repair

U028D.d: Active aerodynamic features change the airflow around the body while driving, for example an extending front air dam, a movable wing or ride height that drops at speed. CARB defines them as active off-cycle technologies, cites grill shutters and speed-dependent ride height as examples and requires counters that record how long they are deployed.
s: Active aero warning message in the cluster
Element does not deploy or retract
Slightly higher consumption at highway speed
c: Element or its wiring damaged by kerbs, snow or debris
Water or corrosion at the module connector
Fuse, supply or ground of module A faulty

U028E.d: U028E concerns a second aerodynamic control module, B, on vehicles that drive more than one active element or split one element into separately controlled halves. Ford's F-150 is a practical example of the latter: its active air dam has a left and a right actuator whose firmware Ford blamed for C0604 logged by the PCM (SSM 51718), and bulletin 24-2404 and its successors cure the warning Active Air Dam System Fault Se
s: Active aero or air dam warning in the cluster
One side of an element stuck or misaligned
c: Wiring or connector of module B damaged near the moving element
Outdated software in module B or the commanding controller
Supply or ground of module B interrupted

U028F.d: A third aerodynamic control module, C, is found on vehicles that combine front elements with rear ones such as a deployable spoiler or an adjustable wing. Sports cars show what these rear parts do: the 2017–2019 Ford GT raises and lowers an active aero wing, and Ford's bulletin 20-2353 deals with that wing touching the body after long storage in its lowered position.
s: Spoiler or wing no longer moves
Active aero fault message, sometimes a speed limitation
c: Wiring chafed or broken at the moving rear element
Moisture in the connector of module C
Fuse, supply or ground of module C faulty

U0290.d: Module D is the last of four aerodynamic control addresses and fits vehicles in which aerodynamics are integrated with chassis functions. Ford's Mustang GTD is such a case: its hydraulic system serves both the suspension and the active aero elements, and service message SSM 55237 lists the warning Active Aero Fault together with suspension and front lift messages, caused by vehicle dynamics module software that repor
s: Active aero fault message
Drive modes or top speed restricted
Aero element stuck in one position
c: Software of module D or the vehicle dynamics controller
Bus or supply wiring to module D damaged
Moisture or corrosion at the connector of module D

U0291.d: With shift-by-wire, the driver's lever, buttons or dial is an electronic module that sends the selected range to the transmission over the network. Gear shift control module B is a second unit of this kind; U0291 means the transmission controller has stopped receiving its messages.
s: Gear selection at the selector has no effect
Transmission warning or flashing range display
Vehicle cannot be shifted out of Park or Neutral
c: Loose or corroded connector at the second selector
Bus line to selector B chafed or interrupted
Selector variant or software not matching the transmission calibration

U0292.d: Electric and hybrid vehicles with a motor on each axle usually give the inverter of the second motor the address drive motor control module B. U0292 means the coordinating controller no longer receives its messages.
s: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Drive system warnings, restricted gear selection
Only one axle driven, reduced power
c: Low-voltage harness of the second drive unit chafed
Blown supply fuse of module B
Connector at the inverter of module B loose or corroded
Inverter or control module B internally failed

U0293.d: The hybrid or EV powertrain control module coordinates engine, motors and high-voltage battery, so many controllers depend on its frames. Ford's 2019 hybrid OBD summary has the battery module set U0293 when HPCM messages are missing for 1 or 5 s, and the brake module set it because wheel torque data are lost; the 2014 list marks it with MIL.
s: Check engine lamp or hybrid system warning
Vehicle does not become ready or will not start
Stop safely now message, loss of power
c: Supply relay or fuse of the hybrid powertrain module (e.g. IGCT relay in frost)
Software in the hybrid module, gateway or receiving module
Connector fault, including grease applied to module connectors
CAN wiring to the hybrid module damaged
Hybrid/EV powertrain control module internally failed

U0294.d: A powertrain control monitor module is a separate supervisor that recalculates torque, speed or driver demand and checks whether the main controller's commands stay within safe limits. U0294 is stored when that supervisor stops communicating, so the plausibility layer is missing.
s: Wrench or drive system warning lamp
Reduced power or limp home
Gear selection refused, especially in cold weather
c: Software of the monitoring or main controller (incl. cold-start behaviour)
Supply, ground or wake-up of the monitoring module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the monitoring module damaged

U0295.d: An AC/AC converter takes in alternating current and delivers alternating current at a different voltage or frequency, with no DC storage in between. In electric vehicles such a stage can be part of a charger: in patent US9973107B2 a matrix stage converts the three mains phases directly to a high-frequency waveform, which an isolating transformer passes on before rectification for the battery.
s: AC charging not possible or interrupted
Charging or power supply warning
c: Low-voltage supply or wake-up of the converter module missing
Bus wiring or connector to the converter damaged
Converter shut down after overheating or a coolant fault

U0296.d: An AC/DC converter rectifies alternating current; in plug-in vehicles the best known example is the on-board charger, which also runs in the opposite direction of an inverter feeding a motor. U0296 means converter module A no longer reports on the bus.
s: ESC or hybrid system warning in the cluster
Pure electric driving not available
Charging from the grid not possible
c: Aftermarket device or Y-splitter on the diagnostic connector disturbing the bus
Outdated software in the converter or inverter module
Supply, ground or bus wiring of converter A faulty

U0297.d: Converter B is a second AC/DC unit, typically an additional on-board charger that raises AC charging power when combined with the first. Patents show how such pairs are coordinated: in Porsche's US10029578B2 one charger leads and the other follows commands received over a communication link, while Hyundai's US10270273B2 has a master controller steering slave controllers for several power modules.
s: AC charging noticeably slower than usual
Charging system warning
c: Low-voltage supply or wake-up line of charger B missing
Communication line between the converters interrupted
Software or configuration does not match the fitted charger variant

U0298.d: A DC/DC converter adapts one direct voltage to another. Hybrids and EVs use it to charge the 12 V system from the traction battery, while some start-stop cars use it to keep the voltage steady for sensitive electronics during an engine restart.
s: Start-stop no longer active
