12 V battery discharging, charge warning
Electronics resetting during engine restarts
c: Converter connector corroded, often from water in the battery area
Blown fuse or missing supply at converter A
Bus wiring to converter A damaged

U0299.d: A second DC/DC converter, B, appears where a single support stage cannot serve every consumer or where two networks are fed separately. FCA documents the code: in PCM reflash bulletins 18-023-19 Rev.
s: Check engine lamp on
Engine does not always restart after auto stop
Start-stop function disabled
c: Supply, fuse or ground of converter B faulty
Bus wiring or connector to converter B damaged
Converter B internally failed, e.g. after overheating

U029A.d: The battery pack sensor module is the electronics inside the high-voltage battery that reports pack current and voltage; many designs house it together with the main contactors. U029A means the battery or vehicle controller no longer hears from it.
s: Wrench or turtle symbol, reduced power
Vehicle does not enable drive or stops charging
High-voltage system warning in the cluster
c: Outdated software in the battery control module or sensor module
Code latched after programming because the network never went to sleep
Moisture or poor contact at the battery low-voltage connector or bus wiring
Battery pack sensor module internally failed

U029B.d: Drive motor control module C is the inverter and controller of a third traction motor, so it only occurs on vehicles with three or four drive motors. Production examples are the tri-motor version of the GMC Hummer EV, which drives its rear axle with two motors, and Rivian's quad-motor R1T and R1S with one motor per wheel.
s: Reduced power warning, one motor disabled
Torque vectoring or all-wheel-drive functions unavailable
Drive system warning in the cluster
c: Fuse, low-voltage supply or ground of module C faulty
Damaged or corroded bus wiring or connector at the drive unit
Software fault or interrupted programming of module C
Drive motor control module C internally failed

U029C.d: Letter D refers to the controller of a fourth drive motor, which presupposes individual-wheel drive. Rivian's quad-motor R1S is the familiar production case: each wheel gets its own frame-mounted Bosch motor, so torque can be split freely between all four corners at any time.
s: Reduced power and loss of torque vectoring
Drive system warning in the cluster
Uneven traction when accelerating
c: Fuse, low-voltage supply or ground of module D faulty
Bus wiring near the wheel drive unit chafed or wet
Software fault or failed update of module D
Drive motor control module D internally failed

U029D.d: NOx sensor A is normally the engine-out or SCR inlet sensor; its control unit puts NOx and oxygen values on CAN. U029D means these frames have stopped.
s: MIL on
SCR or NOx monitor not completed
Engine derate on some trucks
c: Water or corrosion in the NOx sensor module connector or harness
Blown fuse, open supply or ground of the sensor module
Sensor CAN wiring damaged or terminating resistor faulty
Engine control software with start-up timing fault
NOx sensor control unit internally failed

U029E.d: Sensor B usually measures NOx at the outlet, behind the SCR catalyst, so the SCR efficiency verdict depends on it. U029E is logged once its CAN messages fail to reach the engine controller.
s: MIL on
SCR efficiency monitor not completed
Engine derate on some heavy trucks
c: Sensor plugs swapped or not fully seated after service work
Water or corrosion in the NOx sensor connectors
Incomplete or wrong engine control module programming
NOx sensor B control unit internally failed

U029F.d: Some evaporative systems run the leak test through a separate module that holds its own valve, pressure switch or sensor and reports results to the engine controller. U029F is stored when those reports no longer arrive.
s: MIL on
EVAP readiness not set
No noticeable change in driving
c: Damaged insulation or corroded strands in the module signal wire
Corrosion or water at the leak detection module connector
Supply or ground of the leak detection module interrupted

U02A0.d: Although it sits among lost-communication codes, U02A0 is a data error code. The expected slot in the invalid-data series, U04A4, had already gone to particulate matter sensor A, as Ford's 2014 code list and Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg data show, so module D's data fault landed here.
s: Hybrid or electric system warning
Reduced power or no charging
Engine runs more often on hybrids
c: Interface board D delivering corrupted or implausible data
Poor contact in the internal communication chain of the pack
Mismatched software between battery controller and interface modules
Damaged cell sense lead at module D

U02A1.d: A third NOx sensor, C, is fitted where the aftertreatment needs one more measuring point, typically behind a second SCR stage. U02A1 is set when its CAN messages no longer reach the engine controller.
s: MIL on after two drives
Further NOx or PM sensor codes stored at the same time
SCR monitor for the second stage incomplete
c: Engine harness chafed on a hot component such as the EGR cooler
Blown fuse feeding the NOx sensor modules
Water or corrosion at the sensor C connector
NOx sensor C control unit internally failed

U02A2.d: The reductant quality module tells the engine or dosing controller whether the tank holds proper diesel exhaust fluid; in many trucks it is one tank sensor unit with level and temperature. U02A2 means its messages have stopped.
s: MIL and DEF system warning
Countdown to speed or restart limitation
DEF quality and level readings missing
c: Water in the reductant harness connectors at tank or pump
Defective DEF tank sensor unit with quality sensor
Missing supply voltage or wrong software version of the module
Damaged CAN wiring between tank sensor and controller

U02A3.d: The particulate matter sensor behind the diesel particulate filter collects soot on a heated element; its own control unit reports the result over CAN, and the engine controller uses it to judge the filter. U02A3 means those frames have stopped.
s: MIL on
Particulate filter monitor not completed
Derate or inducement warning on some trucks
c: Wrong particulate sensor variant fitted during repair
Chafed harness, blown fuse or corroded connector at the sensor unit
Engine control software with start-up timing fault
Particulate sensor control unit internally failed

U02A4.d: An NH3 sensor reports ammonia downstream of the SCR catalyst, showing whether more reductant is dosed than the catalyst can use. Like a NOx sensor it has its own control unit on CAN; Bosch even sells a NOx sensor that delivers a selective ammonia signal alongside NOx and oxygen.
s: MIL on
SCR system warning
Higher reductant consumption possible
c: Engine calibration expects an ammonia sensor that is missing or different
Heat damage, water or corrosion at the sensor connector
Fuse, supply or ground of the sensor control unit faulty
NH3 sensor control unit internally failed

U02A5.d: At roughly -11 °C diesel exhaust fluid turns solid, while EU type approval asked for usable fluid within 20 minutes of a start at -15 °C, so tank, pump and lines carry heaters. Some systems leave their switching to a separate heater control module that reports state and temperatures to the engine or dosing controller.
s: MIL and DEF system warning
Dosing delayed in cold weather
Inducement countdown if it persists
c: Fuse, relay or supply of the heater module faulty
Water or salt corrosion at the module connector near the tank
Shared bus disturbed by another faulty module

U02A6.d: The Safety Integration Control Module is a name from the SAE code catalogue for which no carmaker publishes a role or a fitted model; the term points to a unit that bundles several safety functions, for instance restraint, braking and driver assistance data. U02A6 means another controller expects its cyclic messages and they no longer come.
s: Several safety or assistance warnings at once
Driver assistance functions unavailable
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Software or configuration fault after programming

U02A7.d: Engine sound control means active sound design: a controller composes or amplifies engine sound from live data such as engine speed and torque and plays it through speakers or a structure-borne actuator, the way Volkswagen's Soundaktor or Kia's Active Sound System do. Where this runs in a separate unit, U02A7 records that unit 1 has stopped sending its network messages.
s: Synthetic engine sound missing in the cabin
More audible drivetrain or road noise
c: Fuse, supply or ground of sound unit 1 faulty
Unit or function not enabled or wrongly configured
Bus wiring or connector to the unit damaged

U02A8.d: A second engine sound control exists where one unit is not enough, for example when interior speakers and an exterior sound source are handled separately or two actuators sit at different points of the body. Active sound design covers both directions: inside it shapes what occupants hear, outside it can give a car a recognisable voice.
s: Part of the engine sound effect missing
Code stored without other noticeable effect
c: Fuse, supply or ground of sound unit 2 faulty
Water or corrosion at a connector in an exposed mounting point
Unit 2 coded as fitted but missing or disabled

U02A9.d: Water-cooled charge air coolers need an electric pump in the low-temperature circuit, normally run by the engine controller as a LIN node. U02A9 means the pump has stopped answering.
s: MIL on
Reduced boost or hesitation at high load
Coolant warning or fan running at full speed on some models
c: Water or corrosion in the pump connector or an open inline connector
Terminals pushed out of the pump connector
Software of the LIN master controller needs an update
Charge air cooler pump electronics failed

U02AA.d: In a parallel hybrid the engine disconnect clutch sits between crankshaft and motor-generator. Ford's patent US9296380B2 shows the layout: with the clutch open, the electric machine drives alone; closed, it lets the engine add torque or be started, and the controller exchanges signals with the clutch.
s: Hybrid system warning, MIL possible
No electric-only driving or engine runs continuously
Rough or delayed engine starts while driving
c: Fuse, supply or ground of the clutch actuator faulty
Harness or connector at the transmission or hybrid module damaged
Software fault in actuator or hybrid controller

U02AB.d: A vehicle thermal management controller coordinates pumps, valves, fans and the refrigerant circuit that keep cabin, battery and drive electronics at temperature; Marelli markets such an integrated module for electric cars, ready for fast-charge preconditioning and OBD compliance. U02AB means this controller has stopped talking to the rest of the vehicle.
s: Several warning messages in the instrument cluster
Climate control or battery conditioning limited
Reduced charging or drive power on electrified models
c: Thermal management control module software needs an update
Fuse, supply or ground of the module faulty
Bus wiring or connector to the module damaged
Thermal management control module internally failed

U02AC.d: Boost control A is the actuator that sets boost, usually a vane or wastegate drive with its own electronics that receives targets and reports status over a data link. U02AC means the engine controller has stopped hearing from it.
s: Check engine lamp
Noticeably less boost and power, engine in reduced-power mode
Boost actuator values missing or frozen in the scan tool
c: Corroded or loose actuator connector, chafed bus wires near the hot turbocharger
Actuator loses its supply or ground (fuse, relay, ground point)
Electronics inside the boost actuator failed, often from heat
Weak 12 V battery causing modules to drop off during cranking

U02AD.d: A second boost actuator appears on engines with two chargers, either one per cylinder bank or in a staged layout where a high-pressure and a low-pressure stage share the work. BorgWarner's two-stage patent describes a valve that shifts exhaust gradually from the small to the large turbine; its setting decides which stage does the work.
s: Check engine lamp
Weak pull in the speed range where the second stage normally takes over
Engine power limited
c: Damaged plug or harness at actuator B, heat-aged insulation
Supply or ground of actuator B interrupted
Replacement actuator not matched or not set up for position B

U02AE.d: The battery coolant pump circulates coolant through the high-voltage pack. Electrically commutated pumps like Bosch's PAD2 carry their own electronics, take a speed request by PWM or LIN and report back.
s: Hybrid or battery warning, possibly with the MIL
Reduced charging rate or electric drive power, especially when hot
Battery temperature rises faster than usual
c: Moisture or corrosion in the pump connector, pushed-out terminal
Pump electronics failed (seized rotor, internal fault)
LIN/bus wire, supply fuse or ground of the pump interrupted
Software fault in the battery or thermal management controller

U02AF.d: In staged turbocharging a valve in the exhaust path decides how much gas passes through the small high-pressure stage and how much goes around it. GM's patent keeps this valve closed in one load and speed region, modulates it in a transition region and coordinates it with the variable vanes; Ford's two-stage patent opens the bypass fully and cuts torque when valve control is lost.
s: Check engine lamp
Boost limited, sluggish response at low and medium engine speed
Engine in reduced-power mode
c: Heat-damaged connector or wiring at the sensor near the exhaust
Fault at the engine controller input

U02B0.d: This code covers the digital position feedback of the second boost actuator. Its A counterpart, U0656, appears in GM's 2025 engine tables: the ECM reads the vane position as SENT frames and fails the link when frames stop updating for more than 6.25 ms while the line sits steadily low or high, or when message errors pile up, 480 failures in 600 samples, rated Type A (lamp on the first trip).
s: Check engine lamp on the first trip
Reduced power, boost no longer regulated by actuator B
Higher smoke or emissions on diesel engines
c: Signal line or connector of the B position sensor damaged or corroded
Position sensor of actuator B failed (often integrated in the actuator)
5 V reference or ground of the sensor missing

U02B1.d: Comfort and convenience displays are touch screens for climate, seats and similar settings, separate from the main infotainment screen. Stellantis calls them CCDM; on the Jeep Grand Wagoneer a front unit (CCDMF) is joined by a rear unit (CCDMR) for the second row, and the front one can lock out the rear.
s: Comfort display stays dark or does not react
Climate or seat settings cannot be changed from that screen
c: Loose or damaged connector behind the display, often after dash work
Fuse, supply or ground of the display interrupted
Display module or its firmware failed

U02B2.d: Where a vehicle carries two comfort screens, display B is normally the second one, the rear panel from which back-seat passengers set climate and seats. U02B2 means that unit has dropped off the bus while display A may keep working.
s: Rear comfort display blank or frozen
Rear climate or seat functions only adjustable from the front, or not at all
c: Harness to the rear display pinched or unplugged in the console or seat area
Fuse or ground of the rear display interrupted

U02B3.d: The driver monitoring module evaluates an interior camera that follows where the driver looks, how open the eyes are and how the body is held, to judge distraction and drowsiness; the EU's General Safety Regulation makes distraction warning mandatory on all new vehicles from July 2026. U02B3 is logged when this module stops talking to the network.
s: Driver attention or drowsiness warning unavailable
Hands-free or lane assistance switched off with a service message
Stored driver profiles not recognised
c: Deep battery discharge or replacement left the module offline
Connector at the camera or module loose, e.g. after steering column or dash work
Driver monitoring module or camera failed

U02B4.d: At the front, radar modules measure range and speed of the traffic ahead, which adaptive cruise and automatic braking rely on; corner units also watch crossing traffic. U02B4 means module A no longer answers the assistance controller.
s: Adaptive cruise and collision warning unavailable
Driver assistance message in the cluster
c: Radar connector behind the bumper not latched, corroded or damaged after a collision
Supply, ground or fuse of the radar interrupted

U02B5.d: U02B5 is set when front radar B stops answering on the network. It is one of the few codes in this group with a public manufacturer case: on the 2022 Jeep Grand Wagoneer, Stellantis STAR case S2208000105 reports Active Driving Assist as not ready while the central ADAS module (CADM) holds U02B5, because connector D1082A of the front long-range radar (LRRF), mounted behind the bumper, was not fully latched; reseating
s: Driving assistant reported as not ready
Adaptive cruise and forward collision warning off
c: Radar connector not fully latched (Stellantis LRRF connector D1082A)
Wiring or radar damaged by a front impact or bumper work

U02B6.d: Rear radar modules are hidden behind the bumper corners at the back and supply blind spot detection, which in its advanced form uses one sensor on each side, and rear cross traffic alert. U02B6 means rear radar A has stopped communicating.
s: Blind spot warning unavailable on one side
Rear cross traffic alert off, assistance message
c: Wiring or connector in the rear bumper damaged, e.g. after a parking knock or bumper repair
Rear radar A failed (confirmed when the fault follows a left/right swap)
Water or corrosion in the radar connector

U02B7.d: U02B7 reports that rear radar B, the second corner unit at the back, has gone silent. Stellantis lists it together with U02B6 for the 2022-2023 Grand Cherokee and Wagoneer models in GPOP review 9100222 and relies on a side-to-side comparison: after a pin unlock the two rear corner radars are exchanged, so the fault either follows the sensor or stays on the harness side.
s: Blind spot lamp on one side stays off or shows a fault
Rear cross traffic alert unavailable
c: Harness or connector on the side of radar B damaged or loose
Radar replaced or swapped without completing the calibration drive

U02B8.d: A third rear radar is only fitted where the usual left and right corner pair is extended, for instance by a sensor watching straight back or along a long body. No manufacturer documents U02B8 publicly or states where module C sits, and its invalid-data partner U05B9 is equally unpublished.
s: Rear assistance functions partly unavailable, assistance message
Cross traffic or exit warning restricted
c: Connector or wiring of radar C damaged or unplugged
Supply or ground of radar C missing

U02B9.d: Rear radar module D completes a set of four rear sensors, a layout that only a few vehicles with extended rear sensing use. No manufacturer documents U02B9 publicly; there is no published fitting position, timeout or lamp rating.
s: Some rear assistance functions unavailable
Message about limited driver assistance
c: Wiring or connector of radar D damaged
Fuse, supply or ground of radar D interrupted

U02BA.d: Hybrid and electric cars cool their power electronics, such as inverter, DC/DC converter and on-board charger, with electric pumps that hang on a LIN line and report their state to a thermal or vehicle controller. U02BA means pump B of that loop no longer answers.
s: Warning for the hybrid/electric drive system, MIL possible
Reduced drive or charging power when the electronics warm up
Pump running constantly or not at all, 12 V battery drained
c: Loose or corroded pump connector, open or shorted LIN wire
Pump power supply or ground missing (fuse, relay, ground point)
Pump electronics failed or pump seized
Pump of another position fitted or controller software outdated

U02BB.d: The purge pump actively pushes fuel vapour from the charcoal canister into the intake, which turbocharged engines need because they often lack intake vacuum. GM fits it to models such as Blazer, Encore GX, XT4 and Silverado 1500 as a separate unit with its own electronics, linked to the ECM by LIN.
s: Check engine light after two drives
Further EVAP or purge pump codes stored
Possible fuel smell; driving itself usually normal
c: Purge pump electronics failed (known GM failure, extended coverage)
LIN wire or pump connector damaged, corroded or unplugged
No supply from the actuator or powertrain relay, poor ground

U02BC.d: The localization and mapping module merges satellite positioning, correction data and vehicle motion signals with a detailed map, so that hands-free or automated driving knows its lane and the road ahead; Bosch offers such a GNSS-based unit for driver assistance and automation. U02BC means this module has stopped communicating.
s: Blind spot alert unavailable, service message in the cluster
Hands-free or advanced driver assistance disabled
Several ADAS and Ethernet codes stored at once
c: Ethernet harness routed too tight, connector strained or not latched
Bent or damaged Ethernet connector pins
Module supply missing or module internally faulty

U02BD.d: The night vision control module evaluates an infrared camera, either a passive thermal unit that sees body heat or an active near-infrared system, picks out pedestrians and animals and passes image and warnings to the cluster or head-up display. U02BD is stored when a listening module, usually the body controller, hears nothing more from it.
s: Night vision display stays dark or the function is unavailable
Pedestrian or animal warnings at night are missing
Matching night vision code stored in the instrument cluster
c: Misaligned or not fully seated terminals in the module connector
Bent pins on the night vision module
Module supply missing or module internally faulty

U02BE.d: The trailer backup assist module steers the tow vehicle in reverse so the trailer follows a curve the driver chooses with a knob; with Ford's Pro Trailer Backup Assist the hitch angle comes from a target sticker filmed by the backup camera or from a trailer-mounted sensor. Ram names its unit TRSCM.
s: Trailer backup assist unavailable
Ram: throttle control message, MIL and rear park assist unavailable
Code stored in several modules at once
c: Module software hangs and the unit drops off the bus (Ram 1500, 2021)
Fuse, supply or connector of the module faulty
CAN wiring to the module damaged

U02BF.d: Many cars spread cabin lighting over several controllers; module B is a second unit beside module A (U024A), for example for ambient strips or a rear zone. Such nodes are usually LIN slaves of the body computer, a single-wire bus of up to about 19.2 kbit/s in which the master can detect nodes that fail.
s: Some cabin or ambient lights stay dark
Colour or brightness of a light zone can no longer be changed
c: LIN wire or connector of module B loose, damaged or corroded
Vehicle configuration does not match the module, module not reset after coding
Lighting module internally faulty or without supply

U02C0.d: J2012 gives the active radiator air flow module its own codes, separate from the active grille shutter modules U0284 and U0285. A Hyundai patent shows the kind of hardware meant: a pair of flaps between bumper intake and radiator, fed by an air guide, whose opening meters the cooling air.
s: Check engine light or warning lamp
Cooling flaps no longer move, slightly higher consumption
c: Water ingress and corrosion at the front-end connector or harness
Flap unit or wiring damaged by stones or a minor collision
Actuator electronics of module A failed

U02C1.d: U02C1 concerns the third networked pump of the electronics cooling loop, pump C, which has gone quiet on its data line. Vehicles with three such pumps assign them to different branches, and which branch pump C serves is the maker's choice; no manufacturer documents U02C1 publicly.
s: Warning for the electric drive or charging system
Reduced power or charging rate under load or heat
Cooling fans running hard
c: Pump connector or LIN wire faulty
Look-alike pumps swapped between positions during service
